name: Nithyasundareswarar Temple, Tirunedungalam
deity: Shiva as Nithyasundareswarar (Nedungalanathar), with the goddess Oppila Nayaki (Mangalanayaki)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Tirunedungalam, near Thuvakudi off the Trichy–Thanjavur road, honours Shiva as Nithyasundareswarar — the Nedungalanathar — with the goddess Oppila Nayaki. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Tirugnana Sambandar, it stands among the Shiva shrines of the upper Kaveri, where tradition says the goddess did penance to wed the lord, and sage Agastya worshipped.

sections.history: Tirunedungalam, near Thuvakudi about 21 km from Tiruchirappalli off the Trichy–Thanjavur highway, is a Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar, counted among the Shiva shrines built on the banks of the Kaveri. Its historical name is Thirunedungalam; the stone temple is of the Chola period and later, in Tiruchirappalli district.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian river-country temple, the shrine enshrines Nithyasundareswarar — the Nedungalanathar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Oppila Nayaki (Mangalanayaki) in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas about the prakara. The walled courtyard and gopuram are typical of the Shiva temples of the upper Kaveri near Trichy.
sections.legends: Tradition tells that the goddess Shakti did penance here, meditating on Shiva to be wedded to him, and the lord came in the guise of a thief and took her hand — a marriage legend that gives the shrine its grace. Sage Agastya is also said to have worshipped at this sivasthalam. Shiva is praised here as Nithyasundareswarar, 'the ever-beautiful lord,' with Oppila Nayaki, 'she without compare,' beside him.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Pilgrims on the upper-Kaveri stretch of the Paadal Petra temples near Trichy include Tirunedungalam among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tirunedungalam the pilgrim comes to a river-country shrine near Trichy. Before Nithyasundareswarar and Oppila Nayaki, the visitor finds the unhurried grace of a Tevaram temple of the upper Kaveri, and the memory of the goddess's penance to wed the ever-beautiful lord.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tirunedungalam lies near Thuvakudi, about 21 km from Tiruchirappalli off the Trichy–Thanjavur highway, in Tiruchirappalli district. Tiruchirappalli is the nearest city and rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
